related_questions.question: What is the best treatment for lung fibrosis?
related_questions.snippet: FDA-approved Drugs for IPF These include nintedanib (Ofev®) and pirfenidone (Esbriet®). These medications are called anti-fibrotic agents, meaning that they have shown in clinical trials to slow down the rate of fibrosis or scarring in the lungs. These drugs are approved for patients with mild, moderate and severe IPF.
related_questions.title: Pulmonary Fibrosis Medications - American Lung Association

related_questions.question: What is the standard of care for pulmonary fibrosis?
related_questions.snippet: Treatment of IPF IPF is currently treated with a combination of antifibrotic drugs and pulmonary rehabilitation. The need for oxygen therapy should be assessed, and lung transplantation is an option for moderate to severe disease in select patients.
related_questions.title: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) - AAFP

related_questions.question: What is the miracle cure for pulmonary fibrosis?
related_questions.snippet: There is no cure for pulmonary fibrosis. Current treatments are aimed at preventing more lung scarring, relieving symptoms and helping you stay active and healthy. Your doctor may recommend medication, oxygen therapy, pulmonary rehabilitation, a lung transplant and/or lifestyle changes.
related_questions.title: 7 Things Everyone Should Know about Pulmonary Fibrosis

related_questions.question: What should you avoid if you have pulmonary fibrosis?
related_questions.snippet: Eat a diet low in sodium (salt), added sugars, saturated and trans fat. Try and get most of your calories from lean meats and fish, fruits, whole grains, beans, vegetables and low-fat dairy products.

text_blocks.snippet: Treatment guidelines for pulmonary fibrosis focus on slowing disease progression, managing symptoms, and improving quality of life. Antifibrotic medications, like nintedanib and pirfenidone, are the primary pharmacological treatments. Pulmonary rehabilitation, oxygen therapy, and addressing comorbidities are also crucial components of management. In advanced cases, lung transplantation may be considered.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on slowing disease progression, managing symptoms, and improving quality of life

list.title: Antifibrotic Medications:
list.snippet: Nintedanib and pirfenidone are approved for IPF and have been shown to slow the decline in lung function. These medications can reduce the risk of acute exacerbations and potentially reduce mortality.

list.title: Treatment of Acute Exacerbations:
list.snippet: Acute exacerbations, characterized by a rapid decline in lung function, may require treatment with corticosteroids, antibiotics, or other medications. In severe cases, mechanical ventilation may be necessary.

list.title: Pulmonary Rehabilitation:
list.snippet: This program includes exercise, breathing techniques, and education to help patients manage symptoms and improve their functional capacity.

list.title: Oxygen Therapy:
list.snippet: Supplemental oxygen may be needed, especially during exercise or at rest, to address hypoxemia (low blood oxygen levels).

list.title: Smoking Cessation:
list.snippet: Smoking is a major risk factor for IPF and can worsen disease progression. Quitting smoking is essential for all patients.

list.title: Vaccinations:
list.snippet: Annual flu and pneumococcal vaccines are recommended to prevent respiratory infections that can exacerbate IPF.

list.title: Management of Comorbidities:
list.snippet: Conditions like pulmonary hypertension, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and obstructive sleep apnea should be addressed as they can impact IPF.

list.title: Lung Transplantation:
list.snippet: Lung transplantation may be an option for select patients with IPF, particularly those experiencing progressive decline in lung function.

list.title: Palliative Care:
list.snippet: Early referral to palliative care can help manage symptoms, improve quality of life, and address emotional and psychosocial needs.

list.title: Nutritional Support:
list.snippet: A balanced diet, including low sodium, low added sugars, and lean protein, can help patients maintain a healthy weight and manage symptoms.

list.title: Monitoring:
list.snippet: Regular monitoring with pulmonary function tests (PFTs) is crucial to assess disease progression and response to treatment.

list.title: Patient Education and Support:
list.snippet: Providing patients with information about their condition, treatment options, and self-management strategies is essential for optimal care.
